title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Add detailed per-priority burst reporting and utilization metrics for Dedicated autoscaler; improves SLO tracing and troubleshooting. No breaking config changes.
body:
Motivation: operators and SREs need finer-grained visibility into how Dedicated autoscaler handles priority classes during burst windows and how that maps to utilization and throughput guarantees. Current metrics are fleet-wide and make it hard to reconcile canary failures and dedicated customer SLO regressions.

This PR implements: 1) per-priority burst accounting (token-bucket level) exposed as metrics, 2) utilization reporting broken down by priority and queue (active, queued, throttled), 3) a new endpoint in the observability service to retrieve priority-level utilization summaries for dashboards and alerting, and 4) small autoscaler behavior refactor to emit consistent labels for reporting.

Design notes: the implementation keeps existing autoscaler semantics untouched (no policy changes) — we only augment observability and internal accounting so routing/decision logic is unchanged. The new metrics follow existing naming conventions: redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_burst_tokens{priority="p0|p1|...",fleet="..."} and redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_utilization{priority="...",state="active|queued|throttled"}. A short-lived in-memory aggregator computes per-minute summaries; long-term aggregation is delegated to the metrics backend.

Checklist:
- [x] Add priority-level tokenbucket accounting in autoscaler core
- [x] Emit per-priority utilization metrics (active/queued/throttled)
- [x] Expose /observability/priority-util endpoint (read-only, for dashboards)
- [x] Add unit and integration tests for metric labels and aggregator
- [x] Update observability docs and dashboards
- [x] Manual QA on staging with synthetic burst traffic

Testing: ran unit tests (see CI) and end-to-end on staging. Synthetic load tests validated that per-priority metrics match internal counters and that no extra latency is added to autoscaler fast-path (microbenchmark shows <1% median increase). There was an initial flake in e2e which required a small fix in test harness timing — CI re-run passed.

Migration notes: operators do not need to change autoscaler config. Dashboards will need to be updated to use the new metrics for priority-level views; default fleet dashboards remain unchanged.

Related: ENG-2048 (observability for dedicated autoscaler), ENG-2102 (priority scheduling follow-ups), SUP-4532 (customer incident where priority HoL masked bucket depletion).

Behavioral summary: no behavioral change to autoscaling decisions. This PR is observability-first: better telemetry to inform future SLO-aware autoscaling work.
